alternatives.root_cause: A bad deploy of accounting rolled out an artifact that cannot start, so the service never began consuming.
alternatives.why_not: A failed start usually leaves crash-loop evidence and startup error logs; nothing in the report suggests a release, and the onset is a clean cutover to silence rather than flapping.

alternatives.root_cause: accounting exhausted memory or threads and was killed/wedged, halting consumption.
alternatives.why_not: Exhaustion normally shows a degradation ramp (slowing consumption, partial traffic, OOM restarts) before silence, whereas the single instantaneous NoTraffic alert with no precursor fits an abrupt stop better.

verdict.summary: The accounting service's process stopped doing work (frozen/suspended) while its container stayed up, so it emitted no spans or consumer activity at all, triggering ServiceNoTraffic with no downstream impact.
verdict.reasoning: accounting is an asynchronous Kafka consumer with no inbound edges in the catalog, so no caller can surface its failure as errors — the only observable symptom is the absence of its own telemetry, which is exactly what fired. The blast radius is confined to accounting alone: nothing upstream degraded, no latency or error propagation anywhere in the frontend/checkout chain, and no sibling consumer (fraud-detection) complained. A silent, self-contained total-stop with zero emitted output is the signature of a frozen process rather than a crash (which usually produces restart churn and startup errors) or a dependency problem (which would produce slow-but-present traffic and error logs). Kafka being absent from the graph means a broker-side stall is also plausible, but that would typically silence other consumers too.
open_questions: Does the accounting container show any log lines at all after onset, or does the log simply stop mid-stream?
Is the Kafka consumer group lag for accounting growing while the partition assignment stays held (freeze) versus being rebalanced away (crash/restart)?
Did the pod restart count or image digest change around 10:38?
Are other Kafka consumers (fraud-detection) still committing offsets, which would exonerate the broker?
CPU/memory usage of the accounting process at onset — flatlined near zero (freeze) or pinned/OOM-killed (exhaustion)?
